bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 100-byte witness makes `parser_fuzzer.c` choose the JSON parser, allocate non-NULL `time_fmt` and `time_key` strings, and install one decoder rule for key `AAA` before passing the remaining 60 bytes into `flb_parser_do()`. In the staged vulnerable checkout `75cdb9c17bc897bdd0882c4311d4fcfb7d5aa6fb`, `flb_parser_json_do()` packs that trailing payload into heap buffer `mp_buf`, aliases `tmp_out_buf = mp_buf`, and enters the decoder block because `parser->decoders` is non-NULL; on the reproduced path, the later line-105 inequality proves that call returned a distinct buffer, so the function frees the original `mp_buf` at line 106 but leaves the variable unchanged. Because `parser->time_fmt` is non-NULL, time resolution continues. The witness-supplied `time_key` bytes are `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 20 20 20 20`, so the embedded NUL is the tenth byte and `strlen(time_key)` yields `slen == 9`. The saved ASan sink at line 136 proves the later scan over the reprocessed map reaches a key whose `k->via.str.size == slen` and whose `k->via.str.ptr == NULL`; that error path frees stale `mp_buf` again instead of only cleaning up the live decoded buffer. AddressSanitizer therefore reports a double-free with the previous free at line 106. The fixing commit adds `mp_buf = NULL` immediately after the first free and also frees `tmp_out_buf` on that NULL-key path.

source.description: First non-harness project parser step that consumes the trailing witness bytes and materializes the heap msgpack buffer later freed twice.
source.value_from: The exact staged 100-byte witness is split by the harness into parser configuration bytes 0-39 and parser payload bytes 40-99. Static replay of the harness shows bytes 0-39 select `format = "json"`, allocate non-NULL `time_fmt` and `time_key`, and create a decoder list; the remaining 60 bytes are passed here as `in_buf` with `in_size == 60`: `7b 20 22 22 3a 2d 4c 20 20 20 20 20 20 2c 22 22 22 22 3a 39 20 20 20 20 20 2c 22 22 3a 22 41 41 41 22 3a 2d 25 53 2e 25 4c 5a 39 39 39 25 53 2e 25 20 20 20 20 20 7d 20 20 20 20 20`.
source.note: The saved allocation stack shows the eventually double-freed region originates from this call through `tokens_to_msgpack()` and `msgpack_pack_map()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The harness turns the exact 100-byte witness into crash-relevant parser state and the trailing payload handed to project code.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Byte 0 is `0x20`, so `GET_MOD_EQ(4,0)` selects `format = "json"`. Byte 1 is `0xff`, so `get_null_terminated(15, &data, &size)` copies bytes 1-15 into non-NULL `time_fmt`. After the separator at byte 16, byte 17 is `0xff`, so the next `get_null_terminated(15, &data, &size)` copies bytes 17-31 exactly as `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 20 20 20 20`; the embedded NUL is the tenth byte, so later `strlen(parser->time_key)` stops there and yields 9. Byte 36 is `0xff`, so a decoder list is created, and bytes 37-39 are `0x20 0x20 0x20`, configuring its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. After byte 39 is consumed, the remaining 60 bytes are passed here as `data,size`.

root_cause.description: When the decoder path replaces `tmp_out_buf`, vulnerable cleanup frees the original `mp_buf` but leaves the variable pointing at freed memory. The later NULL-key error path reuses that stale alias and frees it again.
root_cause.note: The fix adds `mp_buf = NULL;` immediately after this free, removing the stale alias before the later error path runs.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The NULL-key error path frees `mp_buf` a second time after the same address was already released at line 106.
sink.note: The saved crash reports `attempting double-free` on `0x625000002900` at this line, with the previous free at `src/flb_parser_json.c:106` and the original allocation from `flb_pack_json()` on the same call path.

parser_admitted.description: The witness's first byte selects JSON format, so `flb_parser_do()` dispatches into `flb_parser_json_do()` instead of the regex, LTSV, or logfmt handlers.

coarse_trace.summary: The exact 100-byte witness configures a JSON parser with non-NULL `time_fmt`, non-NULL `time_key`, and one `AAA` JSON decoder, then passes the remaining 60 bytes to `flb_parser_do()`.

The trailing payload is packed into `mp_buf`; `tmp_out_buf` initially aliases that allocation, and because the harness created a non-NULL decoder list the decoder block runs. On the crashing witness the later line-105 guard proves that block returned a distinct buffer, which is then re-unpacked into `map`.
Because `tmp_out_buf != mp_buf`, the vulnerable cleanup block frees `mp_buf` at line 106 but does not clear the stale pointer.

Time resolution stays enabled, the lookup length is derived from the witness-supplied `time_key` with `slen == 9`, and the later NULL-key error path frees the same `mp_buf` again at line 136, matching the ASan double-free.

fine_trace.note: Static replay of the exact 100-byte witness shows the harness has already used bytes 0-39 to configure `fuzz_parser`: byte 0 (`0x20`) selects `format = "json"`; bytes 1-15 create a non-NULL `time_fmt`; bytes 17-31 create a non-NULL `time_key` with bytes `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 20 20 20 20`, so the embedded NUL is the tenth byte and later `strlen(time_key) == 9`; byte 36 (`0xff`) creates a decoder list; bytes 37-39 (`0x20 0x20 0x20`) configure the only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. The remaining 60 bytes are then passed here as the parser payload.

Source. `flb_parser_json_do()` consumes the trailing 60-byte payload from step 1 and materializes heap buffer `mp_buf`. The saved allocation stack shows the later double-freed 8192-byte region is allocated on this call path through `tokens_to_msgpack()` and `msgpack_pack_map()`.
Before any decoder runs, the temporary outgoing buffer aliases the original packed buffer exactly: `tmp_out_buf == mp_buf` and `tmp_out_size == mp_size`.

Because step 1 created a non-NULL decoder list, the function enters this decoder block. In `flb_parser_decoder_do()`, the matched-decoder path bypasses the `matched == -1` early return, packs a fresh `mp_sbuf`, and returns it through `*out_buf`; the later branch at line 105 proves that this call produced a distinct buffer (`tmp_out_buf != mp_buf`) on the crashing witness. The code then re-unpacks that returned buffer into `map`, so the later key scan operates on decoder-produced data rather than on the original `mp_buf`.

Root cause. After step 4 replaces the outgoing buffer, this block frees the original `mp_buf` allocation but leaves the `mp_buf` variable live. The fix adds `mp_buf = NULL;` here so later error cleanup cannot free the stale alias again.

The early return is not taken. Step 1 made `parser->time_fmt` non-NULL, so execution stays on the time-resolution path and reaches the later key scan instead of returning immediately after the first free.

The witness supplied `parser->time_key`, so lookup uses that attacker-controlled buffer instead of literal `"time"`. Because the 15-byte harness string from step 1 contains bytes `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 20 20 20 20`, the embedded NUL is the tenth byte and `strlen(time_key)` computes `slen == 9` on the crashing path.

Scanning the decoder-produced `map` from step 4, the loop reaches a key slot whose `k->via.str.size` matches the attacker-derived `slen == 9`, so the size filter does not continue. The saved crash at line 136 proves the next guard sees `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` on this witness. Stage 01 artifacts do not dump the exact malformed key entry, so this step records only the observed branch condition needed to reach the sink.

Sink. The NULL-key error path frees `mp_buf` again even though step 5 already released the same address. AddressSanitizer reports the second free at this line on `0x625000002900`, matching the previous free at line 106.

format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 100-byte witness in `gt_results/arvo_33750/poc` (sha256 `76d05dbf787b9857bb6c7509be0f7ce69abb8f4aeaa8c30f68ab50f2447d1575`) as interpreted by `tests/internal/fuzzers/parser_fuzzer.c`. Byte 0 is `0x20`, so `data[0] % 4 == 0` selects `format = "json"`. Byte 1 is `0xff`, so the first `get_null_terminated(15, &data, &size)` copies bytes 1-15 into non-NULL `time_fmt`. Byte 17 is `0xff`, so the second `get_null_terminated(15, &data, &size)` copies bytes 17-31 exactly as `ff 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 20 00 20 20 20 20 20`; the embedded NUL is the tenth byte, so later `strlen(parser->time_key) == 9`. Byte 36 is `0xff`, so a decoder list is created, and bytes 37-39 are `20 20 20`, configuring its only rule as `Decode_Field` / JSON backend / `do_next` for key `AAA`. After byte 39, the remaining 60 bytes are exactly `7b 20 22 22 3a 2d 4c 20 20 20 20 20 20 2c 22 22 22 22 3a 39 20 20 20 20 20 2c 22 22 3a 22 41 41 41 22 3a 2d 25 53 2e 25 4c 5a 39 39 39 25 53 2e 25 20 20 20 20 20 7d 20 20 20 20 20` and are passed to `flb_parser_do()`. For this exact witness, `flb_parser_json_do()` enters the decoder block, later frees the original `mp_buf` at line 106 because `tmp_out_buf != mp_buf`, and then reaches the `k->via.str.ptr == NULL` error branch that frees the stale `mp_buf` again at line 136. This contract is limited to that exact witnessed byte stream and path; it does not generalize to neighboring byte patterns or other parser or decoder configurations.
